issues.t: CVT shudder, surging or transmission failure
issues.sym: Shudder or judder when pulling away, surging, clunks at low speed, the engine revving without the SUV speeding up, a warning light, or a complete loss of drive.
issues.why: The continuously variable transmission (CVT) can let its belt slip, and the metal dust that creates contaminates the hydraulic controls. A 2021 class action covers 2014-on Outlander Sports, and Mitsubishi bulletin 20-23-001 tells dealers to replace the valve body or CVT.
issues.next: Have the CVT fluid and codes checked at the first shudder. Ask a dealer whether the 10-year/100,000-mile powertrain warranty (original owners) covers the repair.

issues.t: Front crossmember rust lets control arm detach (recall)
issues.sym: Clunks from the front end, wandering steering, or a front wheel that suddenly tucks in because a lower control arm has broken loose.
issues.why: Road salt rots the front crossmember where the control arms mount. Recall 20V-279 covers 2011-2016 models in salt-belt states, and recall 21V-144 added more 2013-2015 vehicles.
issues.next: Check your VIN for both recalls. The dealer inspects the crossmember and seals or replaces it free.

issues.t: CVT software can stall engine at highway speed (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls or loses power at highway speed, sometimes with warning lights.
issues.why: A software error in the CVT computer can drop the gear ratio at high speed and stall the engine on models with a regular key (recall 22V-563).
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN for the recall; the dealer updates the CVT software free. If it still stalls after the update, report it to the dealer and NHTSA.

issues.t: CVT delays acceleration (recall)
issues.sym: The SUV hesitates or is slow to pick up speed when you press the gas.
issues.why: CVT control software could delay acceleration in certain conditions (recall 16V-563).
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall; the dealer reprograms the CVT computer free.

issues.t: CVT fluid leak from loose hose clamp (recall)
issues.sym: Red fluid under the front of the SUV, a burning smell, or slipping and warning lights if the fluid runs low.
issues.why: A clamp on a CVT cooler hose may not have been fastened properly on 2.0L models built from mid-2014 to late 2015 (recall 16V-548).
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall; the dealer inspects and fixes the clamps free. Don’t keep driving with a fluid leak.

issues.t: CVT whine or clicking from bad bearings
issues.sym: A whine, hum or clicking from under the SUV that gets louder with speed.
issues.why: Pulley-shaft bearings inside the CVT can fail. Mitsubishi bulletin 15-23-003 covers 2011 Outlander Sports and calls for replacing the bearings.
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether the bulletin applies; it is handled under the 10-year/100,000-mile powertrain warranty for original owners.

issues.t: Windshield wipers stop working (recall)
issues.sym: The wipers slow down, stop partway or quit completely.
issues.why: Water corrodes the wiper motor through its breather hole (recall 16V-792) and corrodes the ball joint on the wiper linkage so it separates (recall 18V-103).
issues.next: Check your VIN for both recalls; dealers replace the motor and linkage parts free.

issues.t: Accessory drive belt can come off (recall)
issues.sym: A squeal or slapping from the engine, then a battery light, heavy steering or rising temperature if the belt comes off. The engine may stall.
issues.why: Worn pulleys (recall 14V-562) or a cracked belt tensioner flange (recall 18V-069) can let the drive belt jump off.
issues.next: Check your VIN for both recalls; the dealer replaces the tensioner, belt and any worn pulleys free.

issues.t: Heater blower motor stops working (recall)
issues.sym: No air from the vents or the windshield won’t defrost.
issues.why: The blower motor on some early builds can fail (recall 15V-233).
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall; the dealer replaces the motor free.

issues.t: Rear parking brake sticks or won’t hold (recall)
issues.sym: The parking brake does not hold the SUV, or it drags and won’t fully release.
issues.why: Water gets into the rear calipers and rusts the parking brake shafts so they bind (recall 18V-070).
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall; the dealer repairs or replaces the rear caliper parts free.

issues.t: Front passenger seat belt anchor may loosen (recall)
issues.sym: The front passenger seat belt anchor near the floor feels loose.
issues.why: The bolt holding the lap end of the belt may not have been tightened properly and can work loose (recall 14V-744).
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall; the dealer inspects and replaces the fastener free.

issues.t: Faulty relays can stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stalls, loses power or overheats without warning.
issues.why: Some relays in the engine compartment were defective (recall 17V-609).
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check your VIN for the recall; the dealer replaces the relays free.

issues.t: Stalling when pulling away from a stop
issues.sym: The engine bogs or stalls as you pull away from a stop or into an intersection, the D indicator may disappear, and power returns after a few seconds.
issues.why: Several owners reported this on 2015 models, often with no trouble codes. One dealer fixed it by replacing the transmission range (inhibitor) switch.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Have the dealer check for updates and test the transmission range switch. Note exactly when it happens and report it to NHTSA if it continues.

issues.t: Battery goes dead after sitting
issues.sym: The SUV won’t start after sitting overnight or a few days and needs repeated jump starts.
issues.why: Owners reported batteries that drained or never stayed fully charged; some dealers found a weak cell.
issues.next: Have the battery and charging system tested, and a parasitic drain test done if a new battery also goes flat.

issues.t: Automatic emergency braking software error (recall)
issues.sym: Forward collision braking keeps braking after a pedestrian is no longer detected, or brake-related warnings come on.
issues.why: Wrong software was loaded in the forward collision and brake hydraulic computers (recalls 18V-620 and 18V-621).
issues.next: Check your VIN for both recalls; dealers update the software free.

issues.t: Automatic braking activates for no reason
issues.sym: A collision warning flashes and the SUV brakes hard even though nothing is ahead.
issues.why: Owners have filed NHTSA complaints about false forward collision warnings and automatic braking; the cause has not been confirmed.
issues.next: Keep the front sensor area clean and have the dealer check its alignment and software. Report each event to NHTSA.

issues.t: Bluetooth, Android Auto or touchscreen problems
issues.sym: The phone won’t pair or keeps disconnecting, Android Auto won’t connect, or the touchscreen ignores taps.
issues.why: Owners report glitches in the head unit software and phone connection.
issues.next: Check for a software update for the head unit and your phone, delete and re-pair the phone, and try a different cable. Have the dealer look if it continues.

issues.t: Weak low-beam headlights
issues.sym: The low beams don’t light the road well at night.
issues.why: Owners complain the factory low beams are dim or poorly aimed.
issues.next: Have the headlight aim checked first. Cleaning cloudy lenses or fitting higher-output approved bulbs can help.

issues.t: Engine shuts off or loses power while driving
issues.sym: The engine stalls or the SUV loses power at speed, sometimes with warning lights, even after recall work.
issues.why: Owners report stalls on newer models, including some that already had the 22V-563 CVT software update. A cause has not been confirmed for all cases.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Make sure recall 22V-563 has been done, have codes read right after an event, and report it to the dealer and NHTSA.

issues.t: Backup camera picture dim or blurry
issues.sym: The rearview camera image is dark, blurry or washed out in daylight, or a “camera not connected” message appears.
issues.why: Several owners have reported poor camera image quality; dealers often found nothing wrong.
issues.next: Clean the lens, then ask the dealer to check the camera and its connection. Always check mirrors and look back when reversing.
